# Assessment — #490: Remove deprecated channel_lan network + CHANNEL_NAME marker (portals rename cleanup)

_Codebase assessment against 0.13.0-beta.3 (2026-07-12). Effort: **S**._

## Current state (already merged)

Neither shim has been removed yet. (1) The `channel_lan` network is still defined in the skeleton source of truth at /home/user/openpalm/packages/skeleton/system/stack/core.compose.yml:188-192, under a comment that already says "REMOVED in 0.13.0 — migrate custom overlays to portal_net before upgrading"; it is an empty bridge no first-party service joins (network-partitioning.test.ts asserts adapters/guardian use portal_net). It is also listed in the network table at packages/skeleton/system/stack/README.md:67 and in a stale comment at scripts/dev-e2e-test.sh:124. (2) The legacy `CHANNEL_NAME` marker is still in `PORTAL_MARKER_KEYS = ['PORTAL_NAME', 'CHANNEL_NAME']` at /home/user/openpalm/packages/lib/src/control-plane/portals.ts:16, consumed at lines 49-50 (portalNamesFromCompose) and 83-85 (isPortalAddon), with doc comments referencing the legacy marker at lines 64 and 99. No test anywhere asserts the legacy marker is recognized (packages/ui/src/lib/server/portals.vitest.ts only uses PORTAL_NAME), so removal breaks no existing test. (3) The "optional deprecation scan" does not exist, and importantly the migration framework (migrations.ts, incl. the promised channel_lan→portal_net rewrite of user custom.compose.yml advertised in CHANGELOG.md:339-344) was deleted in the four-tree rebuild — documented as finding M7 in docs/reviews/upgrade-migration-review-2026-07-06.md:65 — so the removal currently has no safety net for user overlays. (4) Adjacent cleanup that .github/roadmap/0.13.0/docs-cleanup-plan.md:105-122 explicitly folds into #490: the portal adapter loggers are ALREADY renamed to portal-discord/portal-slack (portals/*/src/*.ts), but the shared health endpoint still reports `service: channel-${this.name}` at packages/portal-sdk/src/base-portal.ts:216 (stale comment at line 107), pinned by portals/slack/src/index.test.ts:511 ("channel-slack") and portals/discord/src/index.test.ts:107 ("channel-discord"), and docs/technical/bunjs-rules.md:96 still shows the old logger names.

## Remaining work

- [ ] Delete the channel_lan network definition and its 4-line deprecation comment from packages/skeleton/system/stack/core.compose.yml (lines 188-192) and remove the channel_lan row from the network table in packages/skeleton/system/stack/README.md:67. The managed core.compose.yml is overwritten from the skeleton in user homes on upgrade (applyHome via reconcileStack), so this propagates automatically.
- [ ] Drop 'CHANNEL_NAME' from PORTAL_MARKER_KEYS in packages/lib/src/control-plane/portals.ts:16 (simplify to a single PORTAL_NAME constant if desired) and update the now-stale doc comments at portals.ts:64 and portals.ts:99.
- [ ] Add a negative test (in packages/ui/src/lib/server/portals.vitest.ts, which already covers discoverPortals, or a new bun test next to portals.ts) asserting a compose service carrying only CHANNEL_NAME is NOT discovered as a portal — this pins the removal.
- [ ] Decide and implement the overlay safety story (the issue's 'optional' item, made near-mandatory by review finding M7 in docs/reviews/upgrade-migration-review-2026-07-06.md:65): a read-only scan of the user custom.compose.yml (customComposeFilePath from home.ts) during performUpgrade/reconcile that detects 'channel_lan' and either (a) appends a human-readable warning to UpgradeResult.warnings (currently hardcoded to [] at packages/lib/src/control-plane/lifecycle.ts:524) telling the user to rename to portal_net, or (b) performs the CHANGELOG-promised one-shot channel_lan→portal_net rewrite (custom.compose.yml is already snapshotted/rolled back by withStackEnvRollback at lifecycle.ts:397-475, so a rewrite is crash-safe). Without one of these, an overlay user hard-fails `docker compose config` post-upgrade with zero warning.
- [ ] Fold in the docs-cleanup-plan step 5 rename: change `service: channel-${this.name}` to `service: portal-${this.name}` in packages/portal-sdk/src/base-portal.ts:216, fix the stale 'channel-<name>' comment at base-portal.ts:107, update the assertions at portals/slack/src/index.test.ts:511 and portals/discord/src/index.test.ts:107, and update the logger example in docs/technical/bunjs-rules.md:96 to portal-discord/portal-slack. (Nothing outside the portals' own tests consumes the health service string — verified by grep.)
- [ ] Fix the stale channel_lan comment in scripts/dev-e2e-test.sh:124 (guardian is reached over portal_net) and consider updating the 'channel-' wording in packages/lib/src/control-plane/config-persistence.ts:243 area comment (already says portal_net — verify only).
- [ ] Optionally add a reintroduction grep-gate to packages/lib/src/control-plane/cleanup-guardrails.test.ts (pattern already established there for other cleanups; 0.12.0 implementation-plan.md:455 called for exactly this gate for the 0.13.0 removal): assert no 'channel_lan' in packages/skeleton/system/stack/*.yml and no 'CHANNEL_NAME' in control-plane source.
- [ ] Add a CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] 'Removed' entry: channel_lan network gone (migrate custom overlays to portal_net) and CHANNEL_NAME marker no longer recognized (PORTAL_NAME only).

## Test strategy

Test-first in three suites. (1) packages/lib (bun test, script `bun test --cwd packages/lib` or root `bun run lib:test`): add the negative CHANNEL_NAME-not-recognized case and the cleanup-guardrails grep-gate before flipping portals.ts; network-partitioning.test.ts and skeleton-guardrail.test.ts already parse the skeleton compose files and will confirm the networks section still validates after removing channel_lan. If adding the upgrade-time overlay scan, unit-test it against a temp home with a custom.compose.yml referencing channel_lan (pattern exists in lifecycle.rollback.test.ts / deployment-scenarios.test.ts fixtures). (2) packages/ui vitest (`cd packages/ui && npm run test:unit -- --run` or root `bun run ui:test:unit`): portals.vitest.ts exercises discoverPortals end-to-end via temp stack dirs — extend it with the CHANNEL_NAME negative case. (3) portal-sdk + adapters (`bun test --no-orphans portals/discord portals/slack packages/portal-sdk`): update the two health-endpoint service-name assertions to portal-slack/portal-discord first, then flip base-portal.ts:216. Full pass: root `bun run test` (aggregate bun suites) or `bun run test:t2` (tier 2, non-UI unit tests). Optional docker-gated check: `docker compose -f packages/skeleton/system/stack/core.compose.yml ... config` still validates (the dev:stack file list in package.json shows the 4-file overlay set).

## Dependencies (0.13.0 open issues)

- none

## Risks

- User custom.compose.yml overlays that attach services to channel_lan will hard-fail `docker compose config` after upgrade — the 0.12.0 CHANGELOG promised an auto-rewrite (CHANGELOG.md:339-344) but that migration code was deleted with migrations.ts (finding M7, docs/reviews/upgrade-migration-review-2026-07-06.md:65). Shipping the removal without the warn-or-rewrite work item reintroduces a silent stack-down failure mode.
- Skip-version upgrades (0.11.x directly to 0.13.0) never ran the 0.12.0 on-disk CHANNEL_NAME→PORTAL_NAME rename migration (finding M6: the migration framework is gone). Managed compose assets are refreshed from the skeleton on upgrade so first-party files are safe, but a user-authored custom overlay declaring a portal via CHANNEL_NAME silently stops being discovered as a portal (isPortalAddon/discoverPortals return false) — guardian gating and portal allowlists change behavior with no error.
- The `service: channel-*` health-payload rename is externally observable on each portal's /health endpoint; anything a user scripted against that string breaks. Grep shows no in-repo consumer beyond the two adapter tests, so risk is limited to out-of-repo tooling.
- core.compose.yml in existing homes only changes when an upgrade rewrites the managed asset; a mixed state (new lib, old compose) is harmless here since removing an unused network is compose-inert until the file is regenerated.

## Original issue body

# #490: Remove deprecated channel_lan network + CHANNEL_NAME marker (portals rename cleanup)

Follow-up to #436 (channels → portals rename, completed in 0.12.0). Two back-compat shims were retained for one release and should be removed in 0.13.0:

- [ ] **`channel_lan` Docker network** — removed from `.openpalm/config/stack/core.compose.yml` (it is currently a deprecated empty bridge, no first-party service joins it). Removing it will break any user `custom.compose.yml` overlay still referencing `channel_lan`; the 0.12.0 CHANGELOG already warns users to migrate to `portal_net`.
- [ ] **`CHANNEL_NAME` compose marker** — drop from `PORTAL_MARKER_KEYS` in `packages/lib/src/control-plane/portals.ts` (only `PORTAL_NAME` recognized). Safe once the 0.12.0 migration has renamed all on-disk compose assets.

Optional: a read-only startup scan that emits a deprecation note if `channel_lan` is found in a loaded compose overlay, to warn users before the 0.13.0 hard removal.
